newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGB, Euroyen futures end weaker, eye Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGB, Euroyen futures end weaker, eye Tokyo.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese Government Bond futures drifted narrowly to end weaker in lacklustre trade.
Dealers said the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) purchasing activities this morning prompted a 10-15 tick rise in futures, but this was later tempered by profit taking.
"Outright issues by the BOJ took the market up a bit, but it was marginal," a local bank dealer said.
The JGB March contract closed at 125.30, down from the previous settlement at 125.62 on Tuesday.
A recovery in Tokyo shares, with the Nikkei 225 clawing back 387.70 points to 19,549.41, had limited impact, dealer said.
"On a regular day, the Tokyo share price rise would have had more impact. Liquidity was too thin," the dealer said.
But the weakness in JGB futures cast a bearish cloud over Euroyen, prompting some early selling.
The key June Euroyen contract ended lower at 99.39 against its previous IMM close at 99.41.
Attention was mainly fixed on Japanese stock fluctuations with most sidelined for the Christmas holidays and unwilling to establish fresh positions for the rest of the year.
The rebound in the Nikkei 225 today partly reduced buying interest in Euroyen, but traders said the contract was supported mid-term by views Japan's economy was still performing poorly.
Eurodollar futures were not traded with U.S. financial markets shut for the Christmas holiday today.
